summary.headline: Aarti Pharmalabs Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to Rs.580 Crores, but PAT fell to Rs.62 Crores from Rs.89 Crores amid forex loss and cost ramp-up.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue was Rs.580 Crores (up 9% YoY) while EBITDA fell to Rs.134 Crores from Rs.141 Crores and PAT fell to Rs.62 Crores from Rs.89 Crores. FY26 revenue was Rs.1798 Crores (vs Rs.1771 Crores), EBITDA Rs.406 Crores (vs Rs.428 Crores) and PAT Rs.176 Crores (vs Rs.257 Crores), with a Rs.33 Crores net forex loss, mostly notional on foreign currency loans. Management guided 15-18% revenue and EBITDA growth over the next three to four years, with CDMO/CMO expected to grow 40-50% in FY27. Margins were pressured by new-capacity ramp-up costs, West Asia-linked raw material and logistics inflation, and weak API/intermediate volumes.

financial_highlights.change: Rs.17 Crores in Q4 per Q&A; mostly notional on foreign currency loans
highest ever quarterly revenue; 43% of turnover
highest ever quarterly; 29% of revenue; FY26 Rs.276 Crores, +32% YoY
Rs.647 Crores per analyst PPT-based calc; FY25 ~Rs.700-772 Crores; API segment 28% of Q4 turnover

segments.name: Xanthine derivatives
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue, 43% of Q4 turnover (management cited Rs.227 Crores); 63% export, 74% beverage customers. FY26 Xanthine sales stated as Rs.792 Crores. Chinese rebate removal and US tariffs enabled price increases.

segments.name: API and intermediates
segments.commentary: 28% of Q4 turnover; split 53% regulated, 30% ROW, 17% non-regulated. FY26 about Rs.600 Crores per management, down from FY25. Intermediates faced cost pass-through difficulty on existing high-value orders.

segments.name: CDMO/CMO
segments.commentary: 29% of Q4 revenue, Rs.155 Crores, a record. FY26 up 32% YoY; 21 customers, 54 active projects (35 commercial, 19 in development). Nearly all revenue from phase 3 and commercial molecules.

guidance_outlook: 15-18% revenue and EBITDA growth targeted over the next three to four years; management declined year-specific guidance because project timing shifts by a quarter.
FY27: CDMO/CMO expected to lead growth at 40-50% per annum.
FY27: API/intermediates expected to grow and surpass FY25 levels, per management.

Xanthine capacity rises from 6,000 to 9,000 metric ton per annum; incremental capacity from end of Q1 FY27 with gradual ramp over next few quarters; management said Xanthine revenue from new capacity could be well beyond Rs.1000 Crores.
Capex of about Rs.400 Crores planned for FY27, similar to FY26; capex intensity expected to fall from FY28 as brownfield projects dominate.
Management expects a step-up in operating costs from Q2 FY27 as Xanthine and Atali phase 1 are fully operational; said margins will not fall below 20%.
Long-term CDMO aspiration of around USD 100 million revenue, with no firm timeline; analysts cited Rs.1000 Crores by FY28-29.
EBITDA recovery from new assets expected to take at least one year; working capital to rise as large CDMO projects are financed internally.
capex_capacity: Atali phase 1 (440 kL multipurpose reactor capacity) expected to be fully operational by end of Q1 FY27, with customer audits cleared; phase 2 starting.
Additional 250 kL at leased site; combined about 700 kL of new multipurpose capacity on books from Q1 FY27 versus earlier base of about 1000 kL.

Dedicated CDMO block at Atali under preliminary design; about 12 months to complete from construction start; potential Rs.250-300 Crores topline from a single block; capex turns of 1.5x-2x for dedicated blocks.
Tarapur Unit-4 steroid block debottlenecked, adding about one-third (about 30%) to capacity; further brownfield anti-cancer and other block expansions planned in FY27.

FY26 capex about Rs.400 Crores (Atali greenfield ~Rs.450 Crores total cited for the project); FY27 capex about Rs.400 Crores split roughly equally across Xanthine, Atali/dedicated projects, debottlenecking and replacement capex, plus R&D.
Investment in peptides and oligonucleotides R&D, not expected to yield immediate results.
demand_pricing: Xanthine: price increases secured mainly in US market; Chinese rebate removal (about 11-13%) and US tariffs (20% US, 25% on China) cited. Raw materials urea and methanol roughly 2x; some other inputs up 30-40%. Management said full cost pass-through not possible.
API/intermediates: existing high-value orders resisted price increases; new inquiries quoted at revised cost basis. Raw material and solvent cost impact about 5-7%.

CDMO: pricing pass-through achieved; inquiry activity improving after 2025 slowdown from tariffs and global uncertainty; active customers flat at 21 for several quarters, with management expecting growth during FY27.
Management said customers are moving away from China and seeking differentiated geographies, supporting new CDMO inquiries.
Management said the company is focused on late-phase and commercial molecules, with early-phase work to be pursued via peptide and oligonucleotide chemistry.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Atali dedicated block for a specific molecule, and what is its revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still exploring the block with customer visibility; it could generate about Rs.250-300 Crores topline from a single block, with dedicated blocks giving 5-10 year visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach Rs.1000 Crores CDMO revenue by FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is to reach it as soon as possible, but gave no firm timeline; it depends on approvals and launches of products still awaiting approval.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there a gap between Q4 CDMO revenue numbers in the call and the PPT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are some untallied trading sales of about Rs.50 Crores; CDMO Q4 Rs.155 Crores, FY26 Rs.276 Crores; Xanthine FY26 Rs.792 Crores, Q4 Rs.227 Crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin not expanding despite higher-margin mix and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Xanthine will need spot-market volumes at lower margin, CDMO commercial products carry lower margins, and the cost efficiencies from dedicated blocks come later; EBITDA will lag top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Atali capex turn and how is Q4 margin pressure explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Dedicated blocks are expected at 1.5x-2x capex turns. Margin pressure from new plant costs, man-hours up 50-60%, and operating costs up 43% YoY and 13% QoQ, with a step-up from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Could a forex hit recur in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said forward contracts are accounted for and nothing beyond six to eight months is open; Rs.33 Crores was mainly notional loss on foreign currency loans, not cash.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from new-capacity ramp-up costs and step-up in operating costs from Q2 FY27; management said margins will not go below 20%.
West Asia conflict raising feedstock (urea, methanol), solvent and logistics costs; API customers resisting price pass-through on existing orders.
CDMO revenue lumpiness and project timing shifts; Q4 CDMO revenue included a Rs.155 Crores consignment carried from the prior quarter.
Working capital build from CDMO inventory, since large customers do not pay advance.
Forex volatility: Rs.33 Crores FY26 notional loss on foreign currency loans; rupee-dollar moves hit rupee revenue in API.
Xanthine pricing: Chinese rebate removal supports prices, but growth beyond the 6,000 MTPA base depends on spot-market competition.
Dedicated CDMO block capex and timing not yet quantified; customer count flat at 21.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and capacity, but cautious and evasive on near-term FY27 numbers and margins. Management repeatedly declined year-specific guidance, deferred on capex breakdown and API pricing, and gave inconsistent segment figures during the call.
key_quotes: We are targeting 15% to 18% growth in both revenue and EBITDA for next three, four years.
We do not want to give a pointed guidance for each year.
I think it will take at least one year from now for the current capexes, which are coming on stream in Q1 to meaningfully contribute to the EBITDA and normalization to happen.
Unfortunately, these large customers do not pay us advance. So we have to finance this inventory ourselves.

growth.why: Management targets 15-18% revenue and EBITDA growth over 3-4 years, with CDMO/CMO guided at 40-50% in FY27; backing is partial via Xanthine (6,000 to 9,000 MT from end Q1 FY27), Atali phase 1 (440 kL) and price increases, but no year-specific total guidance and the Q4 EBITDA decline and 'fully utilizing' capacity note temper confidence.
